purpose: Register high-priority future-boundary routes as auditable route cards with probability gates, abort gates, positive chains, negative chains and prohibited-use boundaries.

nonClaims: does not open calibrated model admission
does not output individual death dates
does not claim effective immortality has been achieved

gateDimensionTaxonomy.meaning: Whether the relevant future technology, repair capability, measurement capability or infrastructure window can exist within the route's assumed horizon.
Whether the subject or support system can reach, afford, use, retrieve or otherwise access the relevant route stage.
Whether the subject can safely adopt the route output after access, including comprehension, consent, integration and execution.
Whether the route can preserve subject continuity over the time span it requires.
Whether the route output can combine with later technologies, recovery systems, identity conditions or governance constraints.
Whether low-probability high-damage failures are bounded by abort gates rather than averaged away.
Whether resources allocated to the route displace safer or more evidenced subject-continuity options.

reviewedArtifactSupport.interpretation: Reviewed artifacts support route-card boundary work only; they do not admit a calibrated model or engineering feasibility claim.

claimBoundary.directClaim: A proper-time differential route can reduce subject-experienced waiting time relative to an external reference time in a conditional metric-redshift scenario.
claimBoundary.supportedClaim: The route is a conditional research protocol for modeling waiting cost, exit, continuity, technology-window and risk gates.
claimBoundary.forbiddenInference: A high time-differential factor does not prove a usable black-hole waiting room, artificial gravity engineering, safe return, or effective immortality.

effectChain.directEffect: Changes the ratio between subject proper time and external reference time.
effectChain.firstOrderEffect: If controllable entry, survival, communication and exit exist, the subject may wait through more external technological time with less experienced time.
effectChain.secondOrderEffect: Exit and adoption gates determine whether matured external technologies can actually improve the next subject-continuity cycle.
effectChain.multiOrderEffect: A wait-exit-upgrade-repeat loop can only become an acceleration route if each cycle improves safety, exit, continuity or adoption probability.
negativeChain: high redshift factor
life support, exit or communication fails
subject continuity or governance fails
tail risk dominates time benefit
route is blocked despite high K

gateCoverage.gateQuestion: Can external technology mature during the reference-time interval without assuming guaranteed progress?
Can a subject enter, remain, communicate and exit without treating a thought experiment as an engineering plan?
Can the subject use the matured technology after exit under evidence, consent and governance constraints?
Can life support, cognition and continuity survive the required proper-time interval?
Does one exit-and-upgrade cycle improve the next cycle rather than merely repeat the same risk?
Do irreversible fall-in, radiation, tidal, control, governance and continuity failures trigger abort before any benefit calculation?
Does route investment displace nearer evidence-based survival, repair, recovery or resilience paths?

abortGates: Unbounded tail risk or unavailable governance stop condition.
Claim depends on engineering feasibility not supplied by evidence.

routeCards.routeName: Biostasis and cryopreservation to future repair

reviewedArtifactSupport.interpretation: Reviewed artifacts support route-card boundary work only; preservation, revival and identity-continuity claims remain blocked.

claimBoundary.directClaim: Biostasis routes attempt to reduce biological degradation or preserve structure while waiting for future repair capability.
claimBoundary.supportedClaim: The route can be modeled as a preservation-quality, future-repair, reversibility and continuity-gate problem.
claimBoundary.forbiddenInference: Cryopreservation, vitrification, organ preservation or neural preservation evidence does not prove human revival, restored identity, or effective immortality.

effectChain.directEffect: Attempts to slow, stop or preserve biological and neural damage accumulation during a waiting interval.
effectChain.firstOrderEffect: Preservation quality changes the probability that future repair systems have a usable target.
effectChain.secondOrderEffect: Future repair and identity-continuity gates determine whether preserved structure can become subject continuity rather than archival material.
effectChain.multiOrderEffect: If preservation and repair improve over time, route value depends on iterative storage quality, recovery technology and governance continuity.
positiveChain: recovery and continuity gates are evaluated
negativeChain: preservation intervention starts too late or damages tissue
critical neural or systemic information is lost
future repair or rewarming remains unavailable
identity continuity cannot be established
route remains archival rather than subject-continuity preserving

gateCoverage.gateQuestion: Can future repair or rewarming technology plausibly address the preserved damage class?
Can preservation be initiated, maintained, identified and legally governed without losing the subject target?
Can any future recovery output be adopted as the same subject rather than a copy, archive or damaged continuation?
Can physical storage, identity records, funding and custody persist over the required time horizon?
Can preservation quality combine with future repair, neural continuity and legal identity systems?
Does irreversible information loss, identity uncertainty or storage failure trigger route downgrade?
Does preservation investment displace current preventive, medical, social or recovery interventions with stronger evidence?

abortGates: No preserved target sufficient for the claimed continuity condition.
No reversible or repairable state definition.
Storage custody, legal identity or consent chain fails.
Route is represented as proven revival or clinical recommendation.

reviewedArtifactSupport.interpretation: Reviewed artifacts support identity-continuity route boundaries only; they do not prove consciousness, uploading, or memory-editing safety.

claimBoundary.directClaim: Subject-continuity routes must preserve or govern the neural, memory, personality, agency and self-model conditions that make extended life belong to the same subject.
claimBoundary.supportedClaim: Neuro-continuity is a necessary gate for many life-extension routes because biological survival without cognition, memory or agency may fail the target value condition.
claimBoundary.forbiddenInference: Neural preservation, memory editing, digital avatars, BCI or cognitive tools do not by themselves prove personal identity continuity.

effectChain.directEffect: Changes neural integrity, memory stability, cognitive agency, self-model continuity and identity-governance variables.
effectChain.firstOrderEffect: Preserved cognition and agency determine whether time extension remains usable effective time.
effectChain.secondOrderEffect: Continuity quality changes technology adoption, consent, recovery and long-term project execution.
effectChain.multiOrderEffect: Stable neuro-identity continuity lets other biomedical, AI and future-waiting routes compound without losing the subject target.
positiveChain: neural substrate and memory remain coherent
future technologies can be understood and adopted
negativeChain: brain injury, degeneration or identity disruption
memory, personality, judgment or agency collapse
extended survival no longer preserves the intended subject
technology adoption and consent degrade
route fails the value boundary even if body survives

gateCoverage.gateQuestion: Can relevant neural repair, protection, rehabilitation, preservation or interface methods affect the continuity variable being claimed?
Can subjects access diagnosis, prevention, rehabilitation, assistive tools, continuity records or support systems?
Can the subject consent, understand and safely integrate neural or cognitive interventions?
Can memory, personality, agency and functional cognition remain stable enough across the relevant duration?
Can neural continuity combine with biological repair, AI tools, preservation, legal identity and social recognition?
Does memory corruption, coercive editing, personality collapse, irreversible coma or false-copy continuity trigger abort?
Does investment in speculative neuro-continuity displace prevention, rehabilitation, accessibility or caregiver support with stronger evidence?

abortGates: Continuity condition is undefined or replaced by a copy/likeness claim.
Consent, agency or self-model is bypassed.
Memory editing, preservation or BCI claim is treated as identity proof.
Route ignores neurodegeneration, injury, delirium or cognitive failure risk.

routeCards.routeName: AI-enabled acceleration of capability and biomedical windows

reviewedArtifactSupport.interpretation: This route currently has domain-level support but no reviewed artifact pack in the priority artifact register; model admission is blocked until AI-route Source Cards are promoted.

claimBoundary.directClaim: AI can lower search, synthesis, design, coordination and decision-support costs in research and subject task execution.
claimBoundary.supportedClaim: AI-enabled acceleration should be modeled as changing technology-window probability, understanding probability, adoption probability, calibration quality and tail-risk exposure.
claimBoundary.forbiddenInference: AI capability, model benchmarks, generated candidates or automation do not prove biomedical efficacy, safe autonomy, longer life, or effective immortality.

effectChain.directEffect: Changes cognitive throughput, candidate generation, research iteration, evidence synthesis, automation and coordination variables.
effectChain.firstOrderEffect: The subject and research ecosystem can notice, understand, test and coordinate more options per unit time.
effectChain.secondOrderEffect: If calibration and governance hold, AI can increase probability of reaching useful biomedical, social or safety windows before failure.
effectChain.multiOrderEffect: Capability acceleration can enter the subject-continuity flywheel only if it improves learning, repair, adoption and governance faster than it adds dependency, error or misuse risk.
positiveChain: AI lowers search and design cost
more candidate technologies and decisions can be explored
useful technology windows become more likely
subject capability and continuity infrastructure compound
negativeChain: AI increases speed without calibration
invalid candidates, hallucinated evidence or unsafe agents propagate
resources shift into noisy or harmful paths
automation erodes agency or creates tail risk
acceleration becomes risk amplification

gateCoverage.gateQuestion: Does AI materially improve discovery, validation or translation windows rather than only produce more unvalidated candidates?
Can subjects and researchers access compute, data, tools, interfaces and support without excluding most beneficiaries?
Can users safely adopt AI outputs with review, consent, accountability, rollback and scope limits?
Can AI workflows remain reliable over long horizons despite model drift, data drift, cost shifts and security failures?
Can AI outputs combine with wet-lab, clinical, governance, human skill and social-support systems?
Do hallucination, unsafe autonomy, dual-use, privacy loss, coercion or systemic dependence trigger abort or downgrade?
Does AI acceleration consume attention, money, compute or institutional trust that would otherwise support stronger subject-continuity infrastructure?

abortGates: AI-generated candidate is treated as evidence without validation.
Agentic system can act irreversibly without review and rollback.
AI route creates unbounded privacy, dual-use, security or autonomy risk.
Acceleration claim ignores calibration, access or equity failure.
